tasks.task: Bootstrap the monorepo from an empty or docs-only repo
tasks.note: Then follow the Shell build order from step 2.

tasks.task: Build the Home screen (S4)
tasks.note: The daily card reads daily-and-statistics' summary; the banner slot follows admob-ads' shouldShowBanner.

tasks.task: Build or change any other Shell screen, overlay or dialog (S1-S15)
tasks.note: Add the data skill of the screen: daily-and-statistics (S9, S10), settings-and-preferences (S11), premium-purchase (S12), game-host-integration (S5-S7).

tasks.task: Build the Settings screen or add a setting (S11)
tasks.note: A new setting is a product change: ask the owner, and a new field needs a save migration.

tasks.task: Sell Premium or change the purchase flow (S12)
tasks.note: Every S12 state screen must pass visual parity; the App Store Connect steps are the owner's.

tasks.task: Add or change ads, consent or a rewarded perk
tasks.note: Ads never interrupt play (N8); the AdMob console steps are the owner's.

tasks.task: Add or restyle a Toybox component
tasks.note: A component that is not in the design catalogue needs the owner's design first.

tasks.task: Change colours, fonts, dark mode or a game's palette
tasks.note: Token values change only with an owner decision; a new palette goes through write-palette.mjs.

tasks.task: Add an icon, a game logo, the app icon or the splash
tasks.note: Look at every generated image; the owner looks at a new logo.

tasks.task: Add or change visible text, a message key or a translation
tasks.note: Shell texts come from the copy deck; fa and ckb need the native review before a release.

tasks.task: Fix right-to-left layout, mirrored icons or Persian digits
tasks.note: Prove it in fa and ckb screenshots against the Toybox RTL design.

tasks.task: Add a route or wire navigation between screens
tasks.note: A new route is a product decision; Back never leaves a live run.

tasks.task: Add a store, an action or a selector
tasks.note: Writes that span sections go through updateAndPublish.

tasks.task: Change what is saved or the save format
tasks.note: A new schema version is permanent for players: frozen fixtures, a Gate-Change trailer, and the kill test.

tasks.task: Build the daily challenge, streaks or the statistics
tasks.note: The daily seed goldens never change.

tasks.task: Start a new game app
tasks.note: Then follow the game build order; the bundle id and store ids are the owner's.

tasks.task: Write or change a game's rules, moves or scoring
tasks.note: Rules are pure and deterministic: examples, properties and a pinned golden.

tasks.task: Add levels, a solver, par, stars, packs or the daily level
tasks.note: Pack tables are generated, never edited; goldens change only on purpose.

tasks.task: Draw or animate a game board
tasks.note: Load the input skill with the board: a playable board needs both.

tasks.task: Add taps, swipes, drags or aim on a board
tasks.note: Legality lives only in the game's intentToMove.

tasks.task: Build a real-time game or a simulate-then-replay phase
tasks.note: Fixed ticks, integer commands, replay tests; the owner judges the feel on a ProMotion phone.

tasks.task: Add or tune sounds, music or haptics
tasks.note: The owner listens on a phone before a sound set is done.

tasks.task: Balance difficulty or add bots and sims
tasks.note: Bands stay proposed until the owner play-tests.

tasks.task: Wire a game into the Shell (Game screen, Pause, Result, run end)
tasks.note: The run end is one updateAndPublish write before S7.

tasks.task: Write or fix end-to-end flows or the screenshot matrix
tasks.note: Flows select by testID only; baselines change only on purpose.

tasks.task: Prove a screen matches its Toybox design screenshot
tasks.note: Every built screen, light and dark, en and fa; never widen a tolerance.

tasks.task: Build, run or smoke-test on the iOS simulator
tasks.note: Release builds of the test variant; look at the screenshot.

tasks.task: Release a game to TestFlight
tasks.note: Nothing leaves the Mac without the owner's word in this session.

tasks.task: Add, upgrade or remove an npm package
tasks.note: Stop and ask before any package that is not in the versions table.

tasks.task: Move to a new Expo SDK or Xcode version
tasks.note: Only when `check-sdk-trigger.mjs . --online --save-facts reports/sdk-trigger.json` (expo-sdk-upgrade) prints `RESULT: FAIL [upgrade-due]`; `RESULT: PASS` means no move is due (stay). All apps in one commit on a branch; the move is done when the same command prints `RESULT: PASS` again.

tasks.task: A quality gate, hook or verify run fails
tasks.note: Fix the code, never the gate.

tasks.task: Fix a TypeScript or ESLint error, or split a file that is too long
tasks.note: Split by responsibility; limits change only with the owner.

tasks.task: Place a new file, package, port or adapter
tasks.note: A fifth workspace or a new vendor SDK is an owner decision.

tasks.task: Something errors, crashes, hangs or renders wrong
tasks.note: Look the first error line up with find-fix.mjs, then load the skill the entry names.

tasks.task: Check or improve performance
tasks.note: The owner's phone is the truth; the simulator only shows regressions.

tasks.task: Review accessibility or VoiceOver
tasks.note: The owner runs the VoiceOver checklist on each release candidate.

tasks.task: Prove the app makes no network requests, or answer App Privacy
tasks.note: Baseline and allowlist changes need the owner.

tasks.task: A golden or snapshot test shows a diff
tasks.note: Investigate first; daily goldens never change.

tasks.task: Commit, tag, report to the owner or ask the owner a question
tasks.note: One question at a time, with a default.

tasks.task: Find out what the spec requires (a screen, rule, feature or game)
tasks.note: Quote spec lines with spec-lookup.mjs, never from memory.

tasks.task: Create, change or repair a skill
tasks.note: After any skill is added, removed or re-described, rerun build-index.mjs --write here.

buildOrders.commands: Every "done when" command runs from the repo root and is written out in full. A `<name>.mjs` command is the script `scripts/<name>.mjs` of the skill named after it in brackets: with that skill loaded, put `node` and the skill's scripts folder in front (inside the skill it is `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/`). The first argument `.` is the repo root: every checker takes the root as an optional positional argument and never as `--root`. `npm run ...` and `node packages/tooling/...` commands run as written. A check is done when it prints `RESULT: PASS`; `SKIP` lines and `NOT APPLICABLE` count as a pass, while exit 2 (nothing to check, bad input) never does. A step whose check cannot pass yet is not done: name it in the report with the reason. `SKIP` lines have exactly two causes: a screen outside `shell-slice.json` (`<S-id> not in shell-slice.json`), or a rule that is not yet due because a later step creates its target (`due at Shell step <n>: <file> not yet created`). Once that step creates the file the rule is strict, which is why steps 6, 7 and 8 rerun some earlier checks and expect no such SKIP line.

buildOrders.slice: A repo without every Shell screen says so in `shell-slice.json` at the repo root: `{ "screens": ["S4", "S11", "S12"], "why": "Home + Settings parity slice" }`, with ids S1-S15 and S11a-S11d. `"screens": []` means a game-first repo with no Shell app; no file means the full Shell and every check is strict. While the file exists, every checker SKIPs (prints `SKIP <file> [<rule>] <S-id> not in shell-slice.json`, not counted) the rules of screens outside the slice, and the rules that need the Shell app itself when `screens` is `[]`; everything inside the slice is checked strictly. The route table never shrinks: a route whose screen is outside the slice points at `NotBuiltScreen` (navigation-and-routing), model hooks navigate normally, and a slice screen still routed to `NotBuiltScreen` fails. During the Shell build above: write `{ "screens": [], "why": "Shell build in progress: no Shell app yet" }` at step 1, change it to `["S1"]` when step 6 builds the splash and the navigator, add each screen id in the commit that builds that screen (step 9), and delete the file at step 10, once every screen is built (the release gates of step 11 fail while it exists). A slice built on purpose (a parity slice, a game-first repo) follows the same rules. Screens outside the slice have no route or view files, but the partial Shell core below is always there. To add the pilot's Game, Pause and Result to a slice that lacks them, follow "The pilot game into an existing Shell slice". **A slice never ships:** `check-navigation.mjs . --complete`, `check-game-app.mjs . --stage complete`, `check-release-setup.mjs .` and `check-store-artifact.mjs ... .` fail while `shell-slice.json` exists or any route uses `NotBuiltScreen`.

Each owning skill repeats its part in its own partial-Shell notes. The test-only pair (packages/shell/src/app/test-only-api.ts and test-only-entry.ts) starts with only TEST_BUILD_SENTINEL (Shell steps 4 to 7), and each member joins when its file exists; DebugScreen and its TestOnlyApi member stay out while S15 is outside the slice.

verifyGreen.intro: `npm run verify` runs its steps in order and stops at the first failure. Its runner (`packages/tooling/src/quality/run-verify.ts`, quality-gates) reads `shell-slice.json`: while the file exists, knip runs without its export and type issue kinds, and `test:sim` is skipped while no game has a `*.sim.test.ts`; each prints a `SKIP` line, and the last line counts them apart (`verify: 11 steps passed, 1 with SKIP lines`, or `verify: 10 steps passed, 1 skipped, 1 with SKIP lines` before the first sim), so a slice run never reads as clean; a run without the slice file ends `verify: 11 steps passed, 0 skipped`. Nothing uses `--passWithNoTests`. On the Shell build (with the slice file as above) the whole of `verify` is green from Shell step 8, and green with no `SKIP` line from step 10 (the slice file is deleted there). Before a step in the "Green from" column, the step below is expected red for the reason given; any other red step is a real failure.
